recap.back_html: A dictionary from parameter names to tensors. torch.save writes it, torch.load reads it (weights_only=True by default since PyTorch 2.6).
Loads matching names and returns missing_keys and unexpected_keys. Nothing raises if no name matches, so always check the result.
Raises even with strict=False. Drop the old head's keys before loading into a model with a new head.
Only the new head. Any other missing key means the backbone did not load.

snippets: torch.save(model.state_dict(), "encoder.pt")
state = torch.load("encoder.pt") # weights_only=True by default since 2.6
result = model.load_state_dict(state, strict=False)
result.missing_keys, result.unexpected_keys
lessons.takeaway_html: Load only the backbone, use strict=False for the new head, and check missing_keys and unexpected_keys every time.
lessons.title: Transfer learning and loading pretrained weights

recap.back_html: Raise the rate from 0 in a straight line over the first steps, so early noisy gradients do not damage pretrained weights.
From the end of warm-up, lower the rate in a straight line to 0 at the last step: (total - step) / (total - warmup).
Batches per epoch, rounded up, times epochs. Call scheduler.step() after optimizer.step() once per batch.
get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(optimizer, num_warmup_steps, num_training_steps); TrainingArguments learning_rate 5e-5, warmup_steps a count or a share below 1.

snippets: def warmup_linear(step, warmup_steps, total_steps):
if step < warmup_steps:
return step / warmup_steps
return max(0.0, (total_steps - step) / (total_steps - warmup_steps))
lessons.takeaway_html: Warm up from 0, decay to 0, count steps as batches times epochs, and step the scheduler after the optimiser every batch.
lessons.title: Learning rates for fine-tuning, warm-up and decay

recap.back_html: y = x @ W.T + (alpha / r) * x @ A.T @ B.T, with W frozen, A (r, d_in), B (d_out, r).
A random, B zero, so the update is zero and training starts from the pretrained model.
r * (d_in + d_out) values per layer: 12,288 instead of 589,824 for 768 by 768 at r = 8.
W + (alpha / r) * B @ A as a new matrix: one plain layer, no extra cost at prediction.

snippets: y = x @ W.T + (alpha / r) * (x @ A.T @ B.T)
lessons.takeaway_html: LoRA freezes W and trains A and B with B at zero, scales the update by alpha / r, and merges into one matrix after training.
lessons.title: LoRA, fine-tuning with a low-rank update

recap.back_html: AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(name, num_labels=..., id2label=..., label2id=...). The new head shows as MISSING in the load report.
Integer IDs: cross-entropy. Floats with num_labels > 1: multi-label sigmoid. num_labels=1: mean squared error.
tokenizer(texts, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=..., return_tensors="pt") gives input_ids and attention_mask.
LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS, target_modules=["query", "value"], ...). Without task_type the new head stays frozen.

snippets: tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
name, num_labels=3, id2label=id2label, label2id=label2id)
batch = tokenizer(texts, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=128, return_tensors="pt")
out = model(**batch, labels=labels) # out.loss, out.logits
config = LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS, r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["query", "value"])
model = get_peft_model(model, config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()
lessons.takeaway_html: Pass num_labels and the label maps, read the load report, use integer labels, call model.train(), and give LoraConfig a task_type.
lessons.title: Fine-tuning a text classifier with Hugging Face

recap.back_html: B- begins an entity, I- continues it, O is outside. "New York" is B-LOC I-LOC.
With is_split_into_words=True, the word index of each token: None for special tokens, repeats for split words.
None gets -100, a word's first token gets its label, later pieces get -100. Test with is None, never truthiness.
The default ignore_index of nn.CrossEntropyLoss (PyTorch 2.15). Those positions add nothing to the loss.

snippets: enc = tokenizer(["Ana", "visited", "London", "staffs"], is_split_into_words=True)
enc.word_ids() # [None, 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, None]
lessons.takeaway_html: Tokenise with is_split_into_words=True, align with word_ids(), label the first piece of each word, and give everything else -100.
lessons.title: Token classification, named entities and subword labels

recap.back_html: The trivial baseline (majority class, or all O), a simple model, and the other fine-tuning strategies, on the same validation set.
Run at least three, report mean and range. The best seed reports luck.
Spans (type, start, end) must match exactly. Precision over predicted spans, recall over true spans.
Score it once, at the end. Every extra look turns it into validation data.

snippets: ["B-PER", "O", "B-LOC", "I-LOC"] # {("PER", 0, 1), ("LOC", 2, 4)}
lessons.takeaway_html: Compare against a trivial baseline and a simple model, report mean and range over seeds, score the test set once, and use entity-level F1 for NER.
lessons.title: Evaluating a fine-tuned model
